PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  THURSDAY, MARCH 19, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:00 PM

Alvaro Castillo, Chair  Todd Lemmis, Commissioner
Michele Ware, Vice Chair  Nicholas Santos, Commissioner
Michael Clemson, Commissioner  Jane Templin, Commissioner

  REVISED

  Planning Commission In-Person Meeting

  Members of the public have the option to email public comments
  to planningcommissioners@longbeach.gov

  Comments may also be provided in the Zoom meeting using the raise hand function or by
  pressing *9 on your phone

  Please dial: (213) 338-8477 / Meeting ID: 934 1096 4133
  https://longbeach-gov.zoom.us/j/93410964133

  Please note the Zoom meeting may encounter technical disruptions, but in-person access
  and public comment will continue to be available in accordance with the Brown Act

  To view the meeting from your computer, tablet, or smartphone
  visit: https://longbeach.primegov.com/public/portal?fromiframe=true

CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54617  Recommendation to receive and file Director’s Report.

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

2.  26-54618  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Planning Commission meeting of
  Thursday, March 5, 2026.

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

3.  26-54660  Recommendation to accept Statutory Exemption SE-25-137 finding the project
  exempt from CEQA under Public Resources Code Section 21080.66 (CEQA

  Page 1 of 4
   PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  THURSDAY, MARCH 19, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:00 PM

  Statute, AB 130) as the project is an eligible housing development under AB 130;

  Approve a Modification to Approved Permit (MOD25-018) for the previously
  approved Case No. 1908-14 for Site Plan Review (SPR19-035) and a Vesting
  Tentative Tract Map (VTTM19-003, No. 82912) for the “Mid-Block” project, aka “the
  center block of the Long Beach Civic Center,” which was approved on March 19,
  2020, consisting of two eight-story buildings with 580 dwelling units, approximately
  40,000 square feet of ground floor retail and 885 parking stalls in two levels of
  subterranean parking; the requested modification would increase the proportion of
  residential in the buildings so that there would be 729 dwelling units and
  approximately 2,651 square feet of ground floor commercial with 817 parking stalls
  in three levels of at-grade parking, and the Vesting Tentative Tract Map would
  change from two ground lots with 13 airspace subdivisions, to only two ground lots
  of 2.04 and 2.55 acres, located on a 4.59-acre site at 321 West Ocean Boulevard
  in the Downtown Plan (PD-30) Planned Development District;

  Recommend that City Council approve an “Other Alternative Compliance Method”
  request pursuant to Section 21.67.080 to the requirements of Chapter 21.67 for the
  project’s compliance with the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance. (District 1)

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

4.  26-54619  Recommendation to accept Categorical Exemption CE-26-011 finding the project
  exempt pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Categorical Exemption, Section 15331
  and 15332 (Class 31: Historical Resource Restoration/Rehabilitation and Class 32:
  In-Fill Development Projects); and

  Approve a Site Plan Review request and adopt the proposed findings and
  conditions of approval thereto, to allow the adaptive reuse of an existing 6-story
  office building into 69 residential units on floors two through six. Of these units, 11
  percent are designated as very low income and 9 percent are moderate income.
  The project includes a rooftop addition of 3,345 square feet, consisting of a trellis
  covered community garden and accessory circulation areas. Minor exterior
  modifications including restoration of the clock tower and minor historic
  rehabilitation to the building are also proposed. The first floor will include new
  areas for mail pick up and a community lounge and the basement will house
  shared laundry facilities and bike and scooter storage. The existing commercial
  spaces on the first floor will remain. The property is located at 115 Pine Avenue in
  the PD-30 Zoning district and is a designated Historic Landmark known as First
  National Bank Building of Long Beach. (District 1)

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

5.  26-54620  Recommendation to accept Categorical Exemption CE-25-131, finding the
  proposed project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)

  Page 2 of 4
   PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  THURSDAY, MARCH 19, 2026
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:00 PM

  pursuant to Section 15303 (New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures)
  of the CEQA Guidelines; and

  Approve a Conditional Use Permit (CUP25-016), and adopt the proposed findings
  and conditions of approval related thereto, for a new building rooftop-mounted
  wireless telecommunications facility for Verizon Wireless, including the installation
  of 20 new panel antennas, 12 remote radio units (RRUs), one (1) four-foot-
  diameter microwave dish antenna, and related ancillary equipment, on a 13-story
  hotel building located at 2640 Lakewood Boulevard in the Willow Street Center
  (PD-27) Planned Development District. (District 4)

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Opportunity to address the Planning Commission on non-agenda items. Each speaker is limited to
three minutes to make their comments unless extended by the Chair.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

ADJOURNMENT

I, Rosa Garibay, City Clerk Assistant, certify that the agenda was posted not less than 72 hours prior
to the meeting.

NOTE: The agenda and supporting documents are available online at
https://longbeach.gov/cityclerk/meetings. If a special accommodation is desired pursuant to the
Americans with Disabilities Act, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 570-6101
or cityclerk@longbeach.gov.
